subject: Computer Science

assessmentTargets.concept: Define the Longest Common Prefix problem and its expected output for given string sets.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: You're given a bunch of strings, and what you need to return is the prefix, which is common amongst all of them.
assessmentTargets.instruction: Ask the learner to state the definition and give an example output.

assessmentTargets.concept: Explain why the length of the smallest string bounds the maximum possible LCP length.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: the first thing you would need to find out is what is the length of the smallest string? Because the longest common prefix cannot be larger than the smallest string.
assessmentTargets.instruction: Prompt the learner to justify the bound using the smallest‑string argument.

assessmentTargets.concept: Describe how a hash set is used to detect whether a character is common to all strings at a given position.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: We have a hash set created. We add h to it... What does set guarantee? No duplicates. If the size of the set is one, you know this character has occurred in number of times.
assessmentTargets.instruction: Ask the learner to outline the steps of adding characters to the set and interpreting its size.

assessmentTargets.concept: Trace the outer‑loop (character index) and inner‑loop (strings) execution and explain the early break condition when a mismatch occurs.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: The outer loop is number of characters you want to process. The inner loop is one character at a time of all the three strings... If the size is not one... we break out... which means... third one doesn't match. So I break out.
assessmentTargets.instruction: Provide a short input set and ask the learner to step through the loops, indicating where and why the break occurs.

assessmentTargets.concept: Explain how matching characters are accumulated into a StringBuilder and returned as the final LCP.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: If the size is one, it means it is repeating in all... we append it to a string builder... After I break out, we return Sb.toString.
assessmentTargets.instruction: Ask the learner to describe how the builder is updated and what is returned when mismatches appear early.

Explain how matching characters are accumulated into a StringBuilder and returned as the final LCP.
